items.title: [2610.24081] Location, Location, Generation: Where You Ask Matters for Generative Engine Optimization
items.summary: Generative search engines provide answers citing sources, and their optimization (GEO) depends on the user's location. The study audited how user location affects the sources cited by ChatGPT and Gemini. ChatGPT localizes results based on declared locations, whereas Gemini follows the network's country, leading to different source visibility. This demonstrates that visibility in generative search is location-specific, requiring audits to consider multiple channels. Consequently, location significantly influences the results generated by these engines.
items.audio_script: From arxiv.org, "Location, Location, Generation: Where You Ask Matters for Generative Engine Optimization" details an audit examining how user location influences the sources cited by generative search engines. The study found that the way ChatGPT and Gemini localize results based on location leads to differing visibility of cited sources. The research audited how user location affects the sources referenced by ChatGPT and Gemini. The methodology involved observing the source visibility patterns when queries are executed from different geographical locations. The findings indicated that ChatGPT localizes results based on declared locations while Gemini follows the network's country, resulting in distinct source visibility depending on the engine employed. This demonstrates that visibility in generative search is location-specific, requiring audits to consider multiple channels. Location significantly influences the results generated by these engines. This necessitates further investigation into the cross-channel optimization of generative search results.

items.title: [1611.01578] Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: A recurrent network is used to generate neural network descriptions, which are then trained using reinforcement learning to maximize expected accuracy on a validation set. This method successfully designed a novel network architecture for the CIFAR-10 dataset that outperformed existing ones in accuracy and speed. Furthermore, the approach was applied to the Penn Treebank dataset, where a novel recurrent cell was created that surpassed the LSTM cell performance. This newly designed cell achieved superior perplexity on the Penn Treebank and was transferable to character language modeling with state-of-the-art results. Overall, the research demonstrates a method for automated and effective neural architecture search using reinforcement learning.
items.audio_script: From arxiv.org, "1611.01578] Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning" describes a method for automating and effective neural architecture search using reinforcement learning. A recurrent network is employed to generate neural network descriptions, which are subsequently trained using reinforcement learning to maximize expected accuracy on a validation set. This approach successfully designed a novel network architecture for the CIFAR-10 dataset that demonstrated superior accuracy and speed compared to existing models. Furthermore, the method was applied to the Penn Treebank dataset, where a novel recurrent cell was developed that outperformed the performance of the LSTM cell. This newly designed cell achieved superior perplexity on the Penn Treebank and proved transferable to character language modeling with state-of-the-art results. This research demonstrates a pathway for automated and effective optimization of neural network structures. Future work will focus on expanding this methodology across diverse large-scale modeling tasks.
